previousCoordinate.reasonReplaced: Legacy-punktet lå omtrent 5,33 kilometer vest for Brekke sluser og identifiserte ikke sluseanlegget eller besøksområdet.

identity.resolvedIdentity: Brekke sluser, dagens firekammer-slusetrapp fra 1924 i Haldenkanalen.
identity.identityProblem: Stedet omfatter en operativ slusetrapp, et tilgrensende kraftverk, eldre slusespor, slusebebyggelse, besøksområder og vannbaserte aktiviteter. Canonical må representere selve 1924-slusetrappen.
identity.splitReason: Slusetrappen er ett sammenhengende kanalanlegg. Kraftstasjonen, besøksområdet, den eldre traseen og Anleggsbrygga er separate komponenter eller ankomstpunkter.

evidence.finding: Q11040669 identifies Brekke sluser at 59.14800, 11.55770 and links the entity to Kulturminne ID 241336-9.
evidence.reason: Provides a named lock entity and stable representative coordinate within the current staircase.

evidence.finding: The heritage identifier resolves the lock installation as Brekke sluser in Halden municipality.
evidence.reason: Official cultural-heritage identity for the lock complex.

evidence.finding: NVE documents the canal system and that construction of Brekke power station in 1917–1924 raised Brekke locks and submerged Krappeto locks after the upstream water-level change.
evidence.reason: Supports the relationship between the current lock staircase, hydropower works and the wider canal system.

evidence.finding: Documents four lock chambers, a total lift of 26.6 metres, the adjacent power station and the lock staircase as an active visitor destination.
evidence.reason: Supports the physical configuration, current use and visitor interpretation.

evidence.finding: Documents 2026 boat operations through the four chambers, Brekkeveien 16 as the visitor address and the lack of scheduled bus service to the site.
evidence.reason: Supports present visitor operations without replacing the lock coordinate with the sales or parking address.

evidence.finding: Provides an independent coordinate near 59.1478, 11.5560 and documents early locks, flood destruction, rebuilding, the 1924 system and timber transport until 1982.
evidence.reason: Independent point and historical control within the same lock environment.

evidence.finding: Identifies the canal and locks between Aspern and Femsjøen and explains that the power station uses the same 26.6-metre head as the lock installation.
evidence.reason: Supports system boundaries and the lock-versus-power relationship.

evidence.finding: Visitor and parking listings place the arrival area around 59.14713, 11.55303, several hundred metres west of the applied lock anchor.
evidence.reason: Useful arrival control but rejected as canonical because it represents parking and services rather than the lock staircase.

evidence.finding: The legacy point is approximately 5330.9 metres west of the current lock staircase.
evidence.reason: Rejected because it has no lock, canal or visitor-object contract.

sourceObjectCandidates.rejectionReason: Matching heritage control; Wikidata supplies the explicit representative coordinate.
Visitor address and parking area rather than lock-complex geometry.
Adjacent operational hydropower facility, not the lock staircase.
Located 5.33 kilometres west of Brekke locks.

rawEvidence.description: Persisted lock entity, heritage, canal chronology, hydropower context, current operations, arrival controls and safety limitations.

decision.nextAction: Applied the named four-chamber lock-complex entity coordinate, retained 1924 for the current staircase and separated power, visitor and earlier-lock components. Continue with stromsfoss_sluser.

notes: The coordinate moves approximately 5.33 kilometres east.
The current four-chamber staircase is the canonical object.
The first Brekke lock phase is described broadly as the 1850s because sources vary in exact completion wording.
The power station, old lock environment, visitor parking and downstream harbour are separate components.
The radius is not a lock, canal, power, property, safety, heritage or access boundary.
